title: SDK auth shim: centralized rotation helpers, SSO refresh flows, and secure local-dev defaults
creator: Asha Patel
description: Consolidate SDK-side authentication helpers across Python, TypeScript, and Go. Provide a small auth shim library that handles: secure default local-dev behavior, API key rotation helpers, SSO token refresh flows for enterprise customers, and concrete examples demonstrating recommended patterns for retries and streaming sessions when credentials rotate. Goal is to reduce support burden and inconsistencies across SDKs while making secure defaults easy for engineers.
acceptance_criteria: Publish an auth-shim package (language-specific: redwood-auth-python, @redwood/auth, redwoodauth) with documented APIs for: loading creds, automatic refresh, explicit rotate(), and context-managed temporary credentials.

Examples for Python/TS/Go demonstrating: local development with .redwood/credentials file, ephemeral SSO token exchange flow, programmatic key rotation without dropping streaming connections where possible.
All language SDKs use the shim for default credential resolution order (env vars -> config file -> OS keystore -> SSO live exchange) unless explicitly overridden.
Include a minimal test matrix (unit + integration) covering rotation during active streaming responses and ensure graceful retry semantics are followed.
Security review completed and documented in Confluence; release notes and migration guide published in SDK docs.
No breaking changes to existing public SDK credential APIs except opt-in for the shim; migration instructions included.
implementation_notes: Design a small surface: load_credentials(), watch_and_refresh(callback), rotate_key(new_key), with language idioms (context manager for Python, async iterable for TS/Go streaming hooks).
Credential resolution order should be explicit and testable. Default behavior must avoid printing secrets to logs and mask any env var dumps.
SSO flow: implement browser-based device code + enterprise IdP exchange helper and a headless refresh token rotation for CI; all flows must support KMS/HSM-backed storage for refresh tokens.

Streaming ergonomics: when refresh is required mid-stream, shim should provide a token-retry hook that can inject new Authorization header into long-lived HTTP/GRPC streams where backend supports token swap; otherwise, attempt best-effort reconnection with idempotency guidance.
Backoff/retry: integrate with existing SDK retry policies. On auth-failure (401/403) attempt up to 2 immediate refresh attempts, then exponential backoff before surfacing error to caller.
Local-dev: default config path ~/.redwood/credentials or .redwood/credentials in repo; default file permissions 600; provide a CLI helper redwood-auth login to create short-lived creds for devs.

Secret handling: recommend environment variable names REDWOOD_API_KEY (explicit), REDWOOD_SSO_CACHE (path), or REDWOOD_KMS_KEY_ID for encrypted storage. Document rotation window and how to perform zero-downtime rotation for Dedicated customers.
Testing: add integration CI job that simulates token rotation during active streaming session; include tests using a local mock server that supports token swap semantics.
Telemetry: emit non-sensitive auth events (refresh_attempt, refresh_success, refresh_failure, rotation_initiated) gated by telemetry opt-in and redact any token values.
Docs: produce three short HOWTOs (local dev, enterprise SSO onboarding, rotating keys in production) with code snippets for Python/TS/Go.
Rollout: behind feature flag SDK_AUTH_SHIM=v1 for first release; default off for enterprise customers until migration guidance is approved.
